newsitem.title: UK: London palladium price calm, no Russian metal seen.
newsitem.headline: London palladium price calm, no Russian metal seen.

text.p: No signs were evident on Friday of long delayed platinum and palladium shipments from major supplier Russia, despite earlier comments from export officials that June 20 would see the start of the 1997 campaign, traders said.
Russia supplies 60 percent of world palladium needs and about 25 percent of platinum, but has been out of the market as an exporter since December due to internal wrangling.
Prices were calm, having soared earlier this month to a 17-year high for palladium and a seven-year peak for platinum as the absence of Russian material severely limited supplies of metal.
"The situation has been fluid for a while so I'm not surprised there has been some more delays," one industry source said.

Another said Japanese trade houses were expecting deliveries to begin in early July. "As the price would be on an average of June prices, they were not expecting anything before that," the source said.

Export delays mounted as new faces appeared at the top of the relevant ministries in Moscow and negotiators were distracted by what was seen in London as a power struggle to control the lucrative PGM export business.
The disbanding of the Ministry of Industry in March set things back even further, sources said.
Platinum and palladium are used in autocatalysts, electronics and chemical processing. Platinum is popular as jewellery, especially in Japan, and palladium is a key ingredient in dental alloys.
Platinum was priced at $415.00/$419.00 an ounce on Friday, about a dollar up on Thursday, and palladium was at $198.00/$200.00, up $6.50.
Dealers also noted that palladium borrowing rates were climbing, but one said this might be indicative of expectations that exports would resume from the leading supplier soon.

To borrow palladium for a month was costing 125 percent versus 100 percent on Wednesday but, confirming the supply tightness should be short lived, borrowing palladium for a year was a relatively cheap 35 percent, dealers said.
More typically borrowing metal for a month would cost around two-three percent, they said.
Gold was fixed at $339.55, just off the previous fixing of $340.20, and dealers said the market was quiet after early selling had taken it under $340.00.
